summary:
ASTROGUARD is an interactive educational platform designed to explore astronaut health and safety during long-duration space missions. Our project focuses on five important physiological areas: cardiovascular adaptation, respiratory function, muscle health, bone health, and fluid shifts.

The website features an interactive astronaut body map, suit and anatomy visualizations, health-analysis concepts, mission-safety information, and a scientific evidence-review workflow.

Our goal is to demonstrate how human physiology, health research, and future monitoring technologies could be brought together in one accessible platform to support astronaut health awareness.

ASTROGUARD is currently an educational prototype, not an operational medical monitoring system. Its interactive visualizations demonstrate the concept, while actual medical measurements and predictions require verified research data, validated equations, and connected sensors.

By placing the human body at the center of space exploration, ASTROGUARD highlights the importance of protecting astronaut health on future missions.
details:
ASTROGUARD is a web-based educational prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It explores how future technology could support astronaut health awareness during long-duration space missions.

The Problem

Spaceflight can affect the human body in several ways, including cardiovascular changes, respiratory adaptation, muscle atrophy, bone density loss, and fluid redistribution. Understanding these effects is important for maintaining astronaut health during extended missions.

Our Solution

ASTROGUARD brings these physiological topics together through an interactive website containing four main sections.

Body & Sensors provides a visual astronaut body map with suit and anatomy views. Users can explore five regions associated with cardiovascular, respiratory, muscular, skeletal, and fluid-distribution concepts.

Health Analysis introduces a whole-body approach to astronaut physiology and demonstrates how future monitoring systems could organize information about different body systems.

Mission & Safety explores crew health awareness, spacesuit sensor concepts, safety alerts, and mission telemetry as potential components of future astronaut-support systems.

Science & Research introduces an evidence-based workflow in which scientific documents, verified datasets, and validated equations would be required before presenting physiological measurements or predictions.

Innovation and Benefits

ASTROGUARD combines astronaut visualization, interactive education, and scientific traceability in one accessible platform. Its central principle is that physiological claims must be supported by reliable evidence.

Current Limitations

The website does not currently provide live sensor measurements, validated medical predictions, clinical diagnoses, or operational safety alerts. These capabilities would require additional research, verified datasets, and hardware integration.

Future Development

Future development could include integrating approved scientific datasets, validating physiological models, connecting appropriate sensors, and evaluating the system for potential mission-support applications.

Our long-term vision is to contribute to a future in which astronauts can better understand and monitor their health while exploring beyond Earth.
